newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris bourse opens 1.47 pct higher, Rhone jumps.
newsitem.headline: Paris bourse opens 1.47 pct higher, Rhone jumps.

text.p: French shares opened higher on Wednesday, bolstered by a big gain on Wall Street, and chemical group Rhone-Poulenc rallied on its first-quarter results.
At 0807 GMT, the CAC-40 was 21.47 points or 0.82 percent higher at 2,624.33. It had opened 1.47 percent higher at 2,641.18 on the back of Wall Street's 2.64 percent gain.
The French market climbed more than two percent on Tuesday after U.S. economic data dampened inflation fears.
Rhone opened 9.1 percent higher at 205 francs after reporting a 6.5 percent rise in first-quarter earnings and maintaining its full-year profit forecast.

Rhone-Poulenc chairman Jean-Rene Fourtou said in a statement the company was still aiming for a 20 percent increase in 1997 earnings per share, before exceptionals, even though this had become more difficult due to a product recall at Centeon.
Centeon recalled products in October voluntarily. Manufacturing is expected to restart soon, with sales and distribution due to resume in the second quarter.
Broker Chevreux de Virieu put Rhone-Poulenc on its recommended list, removing Legrand, down 1.41 percent at 980 francs, dealers said.
There was a block trade of 500,000 shares in electrical engineering group Schneider, up 0.53 percent at 323.70 francs, which was executed at 325 francs.
Pinault-Printemps, up 0.87 percent at 2,423 francs, said first-quarter sales were 5.9 percent higher at 20.25 billion francs.
GAN was down 2.17 percent at 139.90 after reporting a bigger than expected 5.7 billion franc loss for 1996. The share had already fallen more than five percent on Tuesday.
French unemployment fell by 4,800 in March with the unemployment rate staying at a record 12.8 percent.
Lafarge, up 2.29 percent at 383.60, reported a 19.5 percent rise in first quarter sales on Tuesday.

Sanofi, up 1.11 percent at 548 francs, reported a five percent rise in first quarter sales on Tuesday after the close. It finalised the sale of some U.S. assets to Abbott Laboratories Inc for $200 million.
Renault, down 0.51 percent at 136 francs, said on Wednesday it was re-inforcing links with its Turkish partner Oyak through increased cross-shareholdings.
